title: Fast Adaptive Undersampling for Volume Rendering
abstract:
Adaptive  undersampling  is a  method  for  accelerating  the  rendering  process  by  replacing  the  calculation  of  a volume integral  with an interpolation procedure for a number of pixels. In this paper, we propose a method for accelerating  the  volume  integral  calculation  for  the  rest  of  the  pixels,  i.e.  those  pixels  for  which  interpolation can not  be  done  with  sufficient  accuracy.  This  method  requires  two  passes  through  the  input  data. On  the  first pass, rendering is done into a low-resolution texture. At this stage, the values of the volume integral on a set of 
intervals of a  given length are  calculated and saved into a  special G-buffer alone with the pixel’s color. On the second pass, these values are used to determine colors of the pixels. For those pixels whose result is not precise enough,  the  volume  integral  is  calculated  on  one  or  several  intervals,  rather  than  the  whole  ray.  The  proposed method allows one  to accelerate  adaptive  undersampling by a  factor of 1.5 on average,  depending on the  input data
